executive_summary: TechCorp's Information Security Policy demonstrates a strong commitment to cryptographic standards and compliance with ECC framework. The policy outlines specific symmetric and asymmetric encryption standards, hashing, and integrity controls. However, some areas of non-compliance were identified, including the reuse of Initialization Vectors (IVs) for stream ciphers and the lack of secure key management. Overall, the policy provides a solid foundation for cryptographic security, but some improvements are needed to achieve full compliance.
compliant_areas: Use of AES with 128-bit key length for standard data encryption (2.8.3.1)
Use of SOSEMANUK stream cipher with 256-bit key for high security data (2.8.3.1)
Use of Serpent with 256-bit key for block ciphers (2.8.3.1)
Use of RSA with 2048-bit key length for web traffic (2.8.3.1)
Use of Elliptic Curve (ECC) based on NIST P-521 for key agreement (2.8.3.1)
Use of SHA-2 (SHA2-384) for digital signatures (2.8.3.3)
Use of SHA-2 (SHA2-512/256) for advanced zone integrity (2.8.3.3)
violations: Reuse of Initialization Vectors (IVs) for stream ciphers (2.8.3.2, 2.8.3.3)
Insufficient documentation of cryptographic key lifecycles (2.8.3.2)
recommendations: Implement secure key management practices, including secure key generation, distribution, and revocation (2.8.3.2)
Use unique Initialization Vectors (IVs) for each encryption operation (2.8.3.2, 2.8.3.3)
Document and implement cryptographic key lifecycles, including key generation, distribution, storage, and revocation (2.8.3.2)
Regularly review and update cryptographic standards and policies to ensure ongoing compliance with ECC framework (2.8.4)
